title: A dual-barrier sustained-release hydrogel based on Cu-exchanged Y zeolite and sodium alginate for infected wound healing
content: Bacterial wound infection and the growing crisis of antibiotic resistance urgently demand non-antibiotic wound dressings that integrate long-term antibacterial activity and high biosafety. Herein, we designed a dual-barrier sustained-release antibacterial hydrogel (CuY@SA) by embedding Cu2+-exchanged Y zeolite (CuY) into a calcium-crosslinked sodium alginate (SA) matrix. The ordered microporous zeolite acts as the first-stage reservoir to enable intrinsic Cu2+ sustained release via ion exchange, while the alginate network serves as a second physical diffusion barrier to suppress burst release and prolong delivery. The resulting CuY@SA hydrogel eliminated the initial burst and achieved nearly-linear Cu2+ release over 48 h, with an equilibrium swelling ratio of approximately 28 g g−1 in pH 7.4 PBS. In vitro, CuY@SA exhibited over 99.9% bactericidal efficacy against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, while maintaining >98% cytocompatibility with NIH-3T3 fibroblasts at hydrogel concentrations up to 10 mg mL−1. In a mouse full-thickness infected wound model, CuY@SA significantly accelerated wound closure to over 98% by day 14, promoted collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, reduced local inflammation, and caused no obvious organ toxicity or cuproptosis. Compared with the control hydrogel (Cu@SA) containing directly added free Cu2+, CuY@SA showed remarkably lower cytotoxicity and superior in vivo antibacterial activity, confirming the critical role of zeolite in precise controlled release. This work demonstrates that combining an inorganic zeolite carrier with a biopolymer hydrogel provides a simple, scalable, and effective strategy for developing safe and long-acting antibacterial wound dressings. More broadly, it highlights the untapped potential of zeolites as versatile and tunable controlled-release platforms for advanced biomedical applications.
